get.summary: List admins with permissions and pages
get.description:
Returns every admin with role, manager, subordinates and per-page permissions, plus the list of active pages. Also auto-syncs any pages defined in lib/admin-pages.ts that are missing from the database.

**Notes:** No handler-level auth check on GET; the deny-by-default middleware requires an admin session. Returns the full admin roster and permission matrix. Side effect: creates missing Page rows on every call.

_Source: `app/api/admin/route.ts`_

_Auth: `none`_

post.description:
Validates the payload with zod, bcrypt-hashes the password (12 rounds) and creates the admin plus its per-page permissions in one transaction. Unknown pageKeys are silently dropped.

**Notes:** No handler-level auth check; admin creation is gated by the deny-by-default middleware. A handler-level role check is still recommended. Audit-logged when a session happens to exist.

_Source: `app/api/admin/route.ts`_

_Auth: `none`_

400.description: Validation error, duplicate email or bad page key

put.description:
Updates admin fields by id and, whenever permissions or isRootAdmin are supplied, deletes and recreates the whole permission set in one transaction. Passwords are re-hashed with bcrypt.

**Notes:** No handler-level auth check; the deny-by-default middleware requires a session. A handler-level role check is still recommended. Sending permissions replaces the entire set; sending an empty array removes all permissions.

_Source: `app/api/admin/route.ts`_

_Auth: `none`_

400.description: Validation error, duplicate email or bad page key

post.summary: Create an admin activity log entry
post.description:
Writes a manual admin activity log row. The caller IP is taken from x-forwarded-for or x-real-ip and the user agent from the request headers.

**Notes:** The POST handler does not check the session even though the GET on the same file does, so audit rows can be forged. ipAddress is truncated to 45 chars and userAgent to 500.

_Source: `app/api/admin/activity/route.ts`_

_Auth: `none`_

parameters.description: Secondary source for the logged IP address

post.description:
One-shot sweep that distributes unassigned master leads and vendor-onboarding leads using the same sticky-then-round-robin logic as the cron. Only touches rows where assignedAdminId is null, so re-running is safe.

**Notes:** Root-admin only. force-dynamic, maxDuration 300s. Side effect: mass-reassigns lead ownership.

_Source: `app/api/admin/assignment-backfill/route.ts`_

_Auth: `other: session with user.isRootAdmin === true (403 otherwise)`_

parameters.name: scope
parameters.description: Set to 'all' to ignore the time window and sweep every unassigned lead

parameters.name: days
parameters.description: Restrict to leads created in the last N days (BACKFILL_WINDOW_DAYS default); ignored when scope=all

parameters.name: target
parameters.description: Which queue to sweep: leads, vendor, or both

post.description:
Bulk-assigns a list of lead ids to one admin using the sanctioned assignAdminToLeads helper, which avoids bumping MasterLeads.updatedAt.

**Notes:** Audit-logged as ADMIN / ASSIGN. Routing-only write that deliberately does not touch updatedAt.

_Source: `app/api/admin/assignments/route.ts`_

get.summary: Merged fraud and trust audit trail
get.description:
Correlates the fraud registry, order flags, vendor flags and deception-flavoured failure reasons into one time-ordered feed, and rolls up parties that appear more than once as repeat offenders.

**Notes:** Read-only. force-dynamic, Redis-cached for 90s, 2000 rows per source and 500 events returned. No handler-level auth check even though it exposes fraud determinations. Test orders are excluded.

_Source: `app/api/admin/fraud/audit-trail/route.ts`_

_Auth: `none`_

parameters.name: days
parameters.description: Lookback window in days, clamped to 1-365

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: Filter the feed to one event type: fraud_registry, order_flag, vendor_flag or suspicious_failure

example.error: Failed to build fraud audit trail

get.summary: Check if an order's IMEI is flagged stolen
get.description:
Hashes the order's IMEI with an HMAC secret and reports whether a matching Stolen Device entry exists in the fraud registry.

**Notes:** Errors are swallowed and returned as {isFlagged:false} with HTTP 200. Hash secret is FRAUD_HMAC_SECRET, falling back to NEXTAUTH_SECRET.

_Source: `app/api/admin/fraud/check-status/route.ts`_

_Auth: `session`_

parameters.name: leadId
parameters.description: Master lead id to check; 400 if missing

post.summary: Flag an order's device as stolen
post.description:
Creates a fraud registry entry with risk score 100 for the order's IMEI and the customer's hashed phone/email, marking the device as a Stolen Device.

**Notes:** Side effect: writes a permanent FraudRegistry record (deletionType admin_flagged, riskScore 100) that blocks the customer/device elsewhere. PII is stored HMAC-hashed.

_Source: `app/api/admin/fraud/mark-stolen/route.ts`_

_Auth: `session`_

OkErrorDurationEnvelope.description: Job/cron failure envelope `{ ok: false, error, durationMs }`.

leadId.description: Master lead id whose device should be flagged

UnspecifiedObject.description: Response body shape not captured by the source re-audit (only the status code was detected). Any JSON object.

adminId.description: Admin to assign the leads to

firstCouponExpiry.description: Hours until the first coupon expires (default 72)

secondCouponExpiry.description: Hours until the second coupon expires (default 72)

password.description: Plain password, min 6 chars; stored bcrypt-hashed

isRootAdmin.description: Grants every page; defaults to false

role.description: SUPER_ADMIN | MANAGER | TEAM_LEAD | EXECUTIVE | SALES_AGENT | VENDOR_ONBOARDING_AGENT (default EXECUTIVE)

assignmentActive.description: Whether the admin receives round-robin lead assignments (default true)

permissions.description: Array of {pageKey, canView, canEdit}; ignored for root admins

firstCouponExpiry.description: Hours before the first coupon expires

secondCouponAmount.description: Value of the second coupon in rupees

secondCouponExpiry.description: Hours before the second coupon expires

MessageEnvelope.description: Message-only envelope `{ message }`; used for both success and failure responses.

OkErrorEnvelope.description: Error envelope `{ ok: false, error }` used by cron / sync style routes.

role.description: SUPER_ADMIN | MANAGER | TEAM_LEAD | EXECUTIVE | SALES_AGENT | VENDOR_ONBOARDING_AGENT

assignmentActive.description: Whether the admin receives lead assignments

permissions.description: Full replacement array of {pageKey, canView, canEdit}

UnauthorizedSuccessFlag.description: Unauthenticated - no valid admin session. Variant for routes that use the `{ success, error }` envelope.

Unauthorized.description: Unauthenticated - no valid admin session (NextAuth cookie), or the expected token/secret is missing or wrong. For operations whose description says *reconstructed from source*, only the status code was detected in the audit; the body shape shown is the codebase convention, not verified per route.

InternalServerError.description: Internal server error - unhandled failure inside the route handler. For operations whose description says *reconstructed from source*, only the status code was detected in the audit; the body shape shown is the codebase convention, not verified per route.

BadRequest.description: Bad request / validation error - a required field is missing or invalid. For operations whose description says *reconstructed from source*, only the status code was detected in the audit; the body shape shown is the codebase convention, not verified per route.

NotFound.description: Not found - the referenced record does not exist. For operations whose description says *reconstructed from source*, only the status code was detected in the audit; the body shape shown is the codebase convention, not verified per route.

Conflict.description: Conflict - the record already exists or its current state does not allow this change. For operations whose description says *reconstructed from source*, only the status code was detected in the audit; the body shape shown is the codebase convention, not verified per route.

ToParam.name: to
ToParam.description: Window end (YYYY-MM-DD, IST). Defaults to today.

FromParam.name: from
FromParam.description: Window start (YYYY-MM-DD, IST). Defaults to 30 days before today.

cookieAuth.name: next-auth.session-token
cookieAuth.description: NextAuth JWT session cookie from logging in to the admin panel. On HTTPS the cookie name is `__Secure-next-auth.session-token`.

cronBearer.description: `LINODE_CRON_SECRET` as a bearer token — every cron job goes through `assertCronAuth` in `lib/linode/cron-auth.ts`, which reads only this variable (despite some jobs being non-Linode).

unverifiedAccessToken.name: Authorization
unverifiedAccessToken.description: Legacy customer routes: an `accessToken` cookie or an `Authorization` header must be PRESENT, but the value is never verified. Not real authentication.

adsWebhookSecret.name: x-webhook-secret
adsWebhookSecret.description: `ADS_WEBHOOK_SECRET`, sent either as the `x-webhook-secret` header or as a `secret` field in the JSON body. If the env var is unset the route rejects every call with 401 (it does not fall through to unauthenticated access).

webhookSecret.name: x-webhook-secret
webhookSecret.description: Generic `x-webhook-secret` header check for an inbound webhook.

cronSecretBearer.description: `CRON_SECRET` as a bearer token, compared with `bearerMatches` in `lib/auth/secret-compare.ts`. Distinct from `cronBearer`, which uses `LINODE_CRON_SECRET`.
